name: Sentinel Butte
generated_description:
At 3,428 feet, Sentinel Butte is a summit in North Dakota. The Sentinel Butte Trail covers 1.7 miles round trip (out-and-back) with about 134 feet of elevation gain — a gradual walk with modest climbing.

Getting There

The trailhead is at 46.90443, -103.86044 (tap for driving directions). It's roughly 195 miles north of Rapid City, South Dakota. Arrive early on weekends — trailhead lots at popular peaks fill quickly, and cell service is often unreliable once you leave the highway.

When to Go

Late May through October is the main season. Snow and ice linger into spring and return early in fall at this latitude and elevation; in winter this becomes a different, more serious undertaking requiring traction devices and warm layers.

Know Before You Go

The Easy rating comes from the National Park Service difficulty formula, which weighs total distance against elevation gain. Most hikers should budget about 0.5 hours of moving time; add margin for breaks, photos and the descent. Download the GPX track from this page before you go — cell coverage is unreliable in the mountains and a saved route works offline in any GPS app. Conditions change: verify current access, closures and weather with the official land manager before you go. Trail data is sourced from OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).

Looking to link objectives or plan a weekend? Nearby summits include Rocky Butte, Camels Hump Butte and Square Butte — each has its own guide on this site.

faqs.question: How long does it take to hike Sentinel Butte?
faqs.answer: The Sentinel Butte Trail is 1.7 miles round trip with about 134 feet of elevation gain, and most hikers take roughly 0.5 hours of moving time. Add time for breaks and conditions — winter or wet weather can double the trip.

faqs.answer: It's rated Easy using the National Park Service difficulty formula (1.7 miles round trip, 134 ft of gain — about 100 ft of climbing per mile). The elevation profile on this page shows exactly where the steep sections fall.

faqs.question: Where is the Sentinel Butte trailhead?
faqs.answer: The trailhead is at 46.90443, -103.86044 in North Dakota. Use the driving-directions link in the Getting There section above, and note that parking at popular trailheads fills early on weekends.

faqs.question: Are dogs allowed on the Sentinel Butte trail?
faqs.answer: Rules vary by land manager — national parks often prohibit dogs on trails, while most national forests allow them on leash. Check with the managing agency for this trail before bringing your dog, and pack out waste.

faqs.question: When is the best time to hike Sentinel Butte?
faqs.answer: Late May through October for snow-free hiking. Check a summit point forecast before you go — conditions up high differ from the trailhead.

faqs.question: How tall is Sentinel Butte?
faqs.answer: Sentinel Butte stands at 3,428 feet (1,045 meters) in North Dakota.
